name: CitCom Customer Insights
author: CitCom.

sections.description:
CitCom Customer Insights gives you a clear, sales-focused view of everyone who visits your site: logged-in users, anonymous guests, and returning visitors you recognise by email.

It brings page visits, sessions, devices, and history together in one clean admin dashboard, so you can understand who your visitors really are, before and after they register.

Free Features

  • Page visit & session tracking – every page view is recorded by a small request the page sends after it loads, and grouped into sessions that end after 30 minutes without activity. Time on page counts only the time the page was actually visible.
  • Dashboard and unified user/guest list – today’s and this week’s activity at a glance, and a single admin table showing registered users and anonymous visitors side by side. Sortable by visits, sessions, last seen, device type, and more.
  • User & guest profile pages – individual profile pages showing the full activity timeline: pages visited, session history, referrers, device, browser, and OS.
  • CRM Notes – add, edit, and delete internal sales notes on any user profile.
  • Guest tracking (optional) – off on new installs; turn it on under Settings. Anonymous visitors get a persistent browser cookie, and on checkout the guest record is merged into the customer account.
  • Email deduplication – historical guest sessions are transferred to the user account when a matching billing email is detected at checkout, on login, or on account creation.
  • Device, browser & OS detection – lightweight built-in user-agent parser; no third-party service or API key required. Detection is only as precise as the browser’s user-agent string (see the FAQ).
  • Consent-aware tracking – integrates with the WP Consent API and with Cookies Banner & Privacy Suite (WPConsent): when either is active, nothing is recorded and no cookie is set until the visitor grants statistics consent. Known crawlers and automated browsers are ignored.
  • Access control – choose under Settings which roles can view the customer list, profiles and notes. Roles that can edit users always can.
  • Privacy tools built in – visitor IP addresses are anonymised by default (the last part of the address is zeroed), recorded data is included in WordPress’s personal data export and erasure tools (Tools → Export/Erase Personal Data), suggested privacy policy text is provided, and old data is pruned automatically after a configurable retention period (365 days on new installs). Guests who never created an account and have not returned within that period are removed too.

Pro Features

  • WooCommerce stats on user profiles and the customer list – lifetime value (completed and processing orders, net of refunds), order counts, average order value, last order date, and a recent order list (combined logged-in and guest orders matched by billing email).
  • WPC Smart Wishlist integration – see every product a user has wishlisted on their profile, and see every user who has wishlisted a product on the product profile page.
  • Product Insights – dedicated analytics for every WooCommerce product: views, unique viewers, purchases, revenue, and per-product profile pages.

What the free version shows: everything under Free Features, with no limits on users, guests or history. On a user profile the WooCommerce and Wishlist tabs, and on a guest profile the Orders tab, appear as locked placeholders that describe the Pro feature and link to the Pro page; the customer list has no WooCommerce or Wishlist columns, and there is no Product Insights page.

Upgrade to Pro →
sections.installation:
1. Upload the citcom-customer-insights folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install via the WordPress Plugins → Add New screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu.
  3. Navigate to Customer Insights in the WordPress admin sidebar.
  4. Optionally configure tracking preferences under Customer Insights → Settings.

The plugin creates its own tables on activation and leaves the rest of your database alone. New installs start with guest tracking off, IP anonymisation on and a 365-day retention period; a notice after activation points to these settings.
sections.faq:
Does it work without WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce is optional. Without it, the WooCommerce tab is hidden on user profiles and the Product Insights section (Pro) is unavailable. Everything else works the same.

Does tracking require user consent?

If a supported consent management plugin is active (any plugin implementing the WP Consent API, or Cookies Banner & Privacy Suite (WPConsent)), tracking is automatically gated behind the visitor’s statistics consent and no cookie is set before it. Without a consent plugin, visits are recorded by default, so it is the site owner’s responsibility to disclose this in their privacy policy; the plugin registers suggested policy text to help with that.

Why does an iPad show as a Mac, or an Android tablet as a phone?

Device, browser and operating system come from the browser’s user-agent string, with no third-party service. Modern iPads identify themselves as Macs, and many Android tablets as phones, so those sessions are labelled that way. Windows 10 and 11 send the same identifier and are shown as “Windows 10/11”.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. Pages are tracked by a small request the page sends after it loads, which carries no expiring code, so a page served from a cache days later is still recorded. If you turn on guest tracking after a page was cached, that page records guest visits once the cache is cleared.

Will it slow my site down?

Tracking is performed by one lightweight, non-blocking request after the page has loaded, so it never delays the page itself. The visitor-facing script is a single dependency-free file of about 7 kB, loaded in the footer. Database writes are single-row inserts on the plugin’s own indexed tables, and a visitor sending more than 30 tracking requests a minute is ignored.

What data is stored?

Page URL, page title, referrer, visit time, time on page, session records with device/browser/OS and an IP address (anonymised by default: the last octet of an IPv4 address and the last 80 bits of an IPv6 address are zeroed), plus billing name and email for guests identified at WooCommerce checkout. Two cookies are used, both set by the tracking request rather than by the page itself: citccuin_session (session lifetime) and citccuin_guest_id (one year, guests only). All data stays in your own database; nothing is ever sent to an external service.

How do I delete a visitor’s data?

Data recorded by this plugin is included in WordPress’s built-in privacy tools: Tools → Export Personal Data and Tools → Erase Personal Data (works for registered users and for guests identified by email). You can also delete everything at once from the Danger Zone on the Settings page. Old page views and sessions are pruned automatically after the configured retention period, along with guests who never created an account and have not returned within it. Ticking “Delete data on uninstall” removes the plugin’s tables and settings when it is uninstalled.
sections.changelog:
2.8.0

  • Changed: The customer list runs one database pass per page instead of two, with the last device, names and roles each found by a single lookup. Large sites should see the list open noticeably faster.
  • Changed: The daily clean-up deletes old data in batches of 5,000 rows, and now also removes guests who have not been seen within the retention period and never created an account. The privacy policy text says so.
  • Changed: Uninstalling always removes the plugin’s transients, notice dismissals and the viewing capability; the tables and settings are removed only when “Delete data on uninstall” is on. On a network, activating for all sites installs on each site, including sites added later.
  • Added: Two database indexes (visits by user and time, sessions by user and start) so profiles and the customer list avoid full table scans. Added automatically on update.

2.7.0

  • Changed: Visits are now recorded entirely by the tracking request the page sends after it loads. Opening a page no longer creates a session, a guest record or a cookie by itself, so crawlers and bots that never run scripts leave nothing behind, and page caching plugins no longer stop visits being recorded (the request no longer depends on a code printed into the page).
  • Changed: Time on page now counts only the time the page was actually visible, keeps counting after you switch back to the tab, and reports on every tab switch and when you leave. Figures will be larger and more realistic than before.
  • Added: Requests from known crawlers and automated browsers are ignored, and the page address and post being reported are checked against the site. A burst of more than 30 visits a minute from one visitor is ignored.
  • Added: The daily clean-up job removes old guest records and sessions that never recorded a page view, a few hundred at a time, so sites with many such records from earlier versions tidy up over a few days. Guests with page views are never touched.
  • Changed: Guest records are created and updated in a single database statement.

2.6.1

  • Fixed: Dates and times on every screen now show in your site’s timezone using your WordPress date and time formats. Previously some were shown in UTC.
  • Fixed: The dashboard’s “today” and “last 7 days” figures now roll over at your site’s midnight, and the queries behind them use the visit index. The figures are cached for five minutes.
  • Fixed: “Total Guests Tracked” on the dashboard now counts the same guests the list shows: not yet converted to a user, with at least one page view.
  • Fixed: Products Viewed on user and guest profiles groups by product, so tracking parameters in the URL no longer split one product into several rows.
  • Fixed: Order links on profiles open the order whether or not WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage is on. (Pro)
  • Fixed: A note looks the same straight after you add or edit it as it does after a reload. Adding a note now checks the customer exists.
  • Added: Each session on a profile shows where the visitor came from (the first outside referrer), for example a search engine.
  • Added: A new capability, “citccuin_view_insights”, controls who can see the customer list, profiles and notes. Roles that can edit users receive it automatically on update, so nobody loses access; tick other roles under “Who Can View Customer Insights” on the Settings page to grant view-only access (only roles that can already see the Users list are offered). Settings still need the Manage Options capability.
  • Added: A short notice after installation pointing to the guest tracking setting, shown until the settings are saved once. New installs start with guest tracking off, IP anonymisation on and a 365-day retention period.
  • Added: Every text in the plugin can now be translated, including the admin script; a translation template ships in the languages folder.
  • Changed: Windows is labelled “Windows 10/11”, since browsers do not say which. See the FAQ on tablet detection.
  • Changed: Icon-only buttons on notes have accessible labels.

2.6.0

  • Changed: The free and Pro versions are now built from one codebase. The free version contains no Pro code at all; the Pro version adds its features on top of the same free plugin.
  • Changed (Pro): If your Pro licence expires or is cancelled you are no longer redirected away from the plugin’s screens. Tracking, the customer list, profiles, notes and settings keep working as in the free version; WooCommerce stats, wishlist data and Product Insights pause until the licence is active again, and a notice on the plugin’s pages tells you why.
  • Changed (Pro): The guest tracking setting, role exclusions, data retention, IP anonymisation, delete-on-uninstall and the Danger Zone no longer need a licence. They have always been part of the free version.
  • Changed (free): The Orders tab on guest profiles now says that order history is a Pro feature, instead of showing an empty list.
  • Added: A short note on the Settings page describing what Pro adds, with a link.

2.5.3

  • Fixed: The role and activity filters are back above the customer list. You can show all users, users and guests together, guests only, or a single role, and filter by recent activity.
  • Fixed: The two guest cards on the dashboard are now hidden when guest tracking is switched off, instead of showing greyed out with a “DEACTIVATED” label.
  • Fixed: Removed invisible characters at the start of some plugin files that could cause “headers already sent” warnings on some servers.
  • Changed: Declared compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage and the cart and checkout blocks, so WooCommerce no longer lists the plugin as untested.
  • Changed: The database structure is now checked only after a plugin update instead of on every page load. Existing data is not touched.
  • Changed: The visitor’s session token is no longer printed in the page source.
  • Changed: The minimum PHP version is now 8.0. The plugin already needed PHP 8.0 to run; the stated requirement now matches.

2.5.2

  • Changed: Confirmed compatibility with WordPress 7.1; full test pass of the dashboard, list table filters, settings, user/guest profiles, tracking endpoints, privacy export/erase, and scheduled data pruning.

2.5.1

  • Changed: Reworded the plugin description and screenshot captions for clarity.

2.5.0

  • Security/Review: all remaining database queries now pass table identifiers through the %i placeholder in $wpdb->prepare(); the user/guest list query was rebuilt as a fully parameterised statement.
  • Changed: removed the last raw <style> output — all admin CSS/JS is loaded via wp_enqueue_style/wp_enqueue_script, and the Danger Zone confirmation moved from an inline onsubmit attribute into the admin script.
  • Changed: stopped invoking the third-party WPConsent filter for cookie-name discovery; the name is read from WPConsent’s settings with a cookie-scan fallback.
  • Added: WordPress privacy integration — suggested privacy policy text, personal data exporter and eraser covering visits, sessions, guest records, CRM notes and last-login meta.
  • Changed: IP anonymisation is now ON by default for new installs; client IP is read from REMOTE_ADDR only (use the citccuin_client_ip filter behind a trusted reverse proxy).
  • Added: WooCommerce checkout guest enrichment/merge hooks are now registered in the free version, matching the documented behaviour.
  • Fixed: the daily pruning cron event is now removed on deactivation and uninstall.
  • Changed: CRM Notes are now listed as a free feature (they were always functional in the free version).

2.4.3

  • Fixed: Added phpcs:disable annotations for DirectDatabaseQuery warnings in page-dashboard.php and page-settings.php to resolve WordPress Plugin Check findings.

2.4.2

  • Fixed: Fatal error on user/guest profile pages — class_exists() guards added before CITCCUIN_WooCommerce and CITCCUIN_Wishlist calls in class-citccuin-admin.php.

2.4.1

  • Fixed: register_menu() now captures page hooks so admin pages are correctly targeted by the load-{hook} action.

2.4.0

  • Changed: Moved all top-level plugin functions into class static methods — removes the function_exists() guards that WP.org flagged in review.

2.3.0

  • Fixed: Danger Zone (Clear All Tracking Data) is no longer hidden behind a Pro-only flag — the feature was already fully functional, only the UI was gated.
  • Fixed: Naming consistency — third-party WPConsent hook usage now properly annotated; internal bootstrap functions renamed to the citccuin_ prefix.
  • Fixed: All database queries that reference table names now use $wpdb->prepare() with the %i identifier placeholder instead of raw string concatenation.
  • Changed: Requires at least WordPress 6.2 (needed for the %i placeholder used in the SQL fixes above).

2.1.10

  • Fixed: Prevent “Cannot redeclare” fatal error when free and premium plugins are briefly both active during upgrade activation.

2.1.6

  • Lite (WP.org): Removed Pro-only classes (WooCommerce stats, Wishlist, Product Insights, Freemius SDK). This version contains only the free tracking and CRM dashboard features.
  • Changed: Plugin renamed to CitCom Customer Insights.
  • Fixed: Updated Plugin URI.

2.1.5

  • Fixed: Plugin Check compliance updates.

2.1.4

  • Fixed: Plugin Check compliance — added inline phpcs:disable annotations to all plugin-owned class files.

2.1.3

  • Fixed: Moved all PHPCS suppressions to inline phpcs:disable comments in view files and list table class. Restored missing global $wpdb declaration in dashboard view.

2.1.2

  • Fixed: WordPress.org plugin check compliance — added phpcs.xml; added missing translators comments; fixed unescaped output; added phpcs:ignore annotations for read-only display params.

2.1.1

  • Fixed: Data cleanup and cron removal execute correctly on plugin deletion.

2.1.0

  • Added: Lite/Pro split — free tracking and CRM dashboard features available to all users. Pro features (WooCommerce stats, Wishlist, CRM Notes, Product Insights) available via upgrade.
  • Added: CUI_Features class — centralised feature gates with inline upgrade notices on all Pro sections.

2.0.1

  • Added: Wishlist tab on per-product profile page — lists every registered user who has saved that product, with avatar, name, email, and date added.
  • Added: Wishlisted stat card on per-product profile showing total unique wishlister count.
  • Added: Wishlisted column on the Product Insights list table, sortable by wishlister count (ascending and descending).

1.1.1

  • Added: Product Insights — dedicated analytics list and per-product profile pages for WooCommerce products.
  • Added: Product list with sortable columns: Views, Unique Viewers, Purchases, Revenue, Last Viewed.
  • Added: Per-product profile with Viewers tab (registered users + guests) and Purchasers tab.
  • Added: Category filter and “Popular (last 7 days)” quick-filter on the product list.
  • Added: Branded Insights button injected into the native WooCommerce product list.

1.1.0

  • Added: WPConsent integration — tracking automatically respects statistics consent when Cookies Banner & Privacy Suite is active.
  • Added: JS tracker listens for wpconsent_consent_processed event to activate tracking mid-page after consent is given.
  • Changed: Tracker script always enqueued; consent gate enforced server-side in the AJAX handler.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Page visit and session tracking for registered users and guests.
  • Unified user/guest list table with sortable columns.
  • Individual user and guest profile pages with activity timeline.
  • Guest cookie management with checkout enrichment and guest-to-user transfer on login.
  • Email-based deduplication and historical session merging.
  • WooCommerce combined order stats (logged-in + guest orders by billing email).
  • CRM Notes on user profiles.
  • WPC Smart Wishlist integration.
  • Device, browser, and OS detection via built-in user-agent parser.
  • Settings page (guest tracking, role exclusions, data retention, IP anonymisation, Danger Zone).

upgrade_notice.2.8.0: Performance release: the customer list opens faster on large sites, clean-up runs in batches, and two indexes are added automatically. No data is changed. Pro: lifetime value now counts completed and processing orders net of refunds, so some figures will be lower.
upgrade_notice.2.7.0: Tracking release: visits are recorded by the page's tracking request only, so caching plugins and bots no longer cause missed or ghost records. Time on page is now real visible time. No data is changed. Pro: released to the beta channel first.
upgrade_notice.2.6.1: Admin correctness release: times in your site's timezone, dashboard figures that roll over at midnight, session referrers, a view-only capability, translations. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.2.6.0: The free and Pro versions now come from one codebase. Pro: an expired licence no longer locks you out; the plugin falls back to the free features until you renew.

upgrade_notice.2.5.0: Privacy and review-compliance release: WordPress export/erase support, IP anonymisation on by default, fully parameterised SQL, cron cleanup on deactivation. Recommended for all users.
upgrade_notice.2.1.2: Maintenance release — resolves all WordPress.org Plugin Check tool findings. Recommended for anyone planning to submit to the WordPress Plugin Directory.
upgrade_notice.2.1.1: Maintenance release — no user-facing changes. Recommended for all users.
